question: Can a learned body prediction help full-photo localization without replacing photographic boundaries or material identity?

protocol.model: Frozen candidate out-of-fold body probabilities from corrected-family study; no retraining or new model selection.

proposal.component: largest by pixel count; deterministic scan order for ties
proposal.padding: 10% of selected component width/height on each side, clipped to photograph
proposal.coordinates: Network cell edges through the recorded full-photo letterbox window; padded-image pixels excluded by source-centre bounds.

arms: production: unchanged full-photo RGB cropper and solver
body-roi: body-derived rectangle only, unchanged RGB cropper/classifier and solver inside that rectangle
protocol.comparison: Fresh solves in both arms, alternating order by photo index. Ten-second fitting budget per attempt; cropping and inference are not included in that budget. No per-photo threshold tuning, mask replacement, reference corners, known slit counts or saved templates.
protocol.fallbackPolicy: Retain production whenever it supplies any crop, including a needs-review crop. Otherwise use the body-roi result. Report this separately; no selection by reconstruction score.
validation: Same crop support checks, geometry checks, independent exported rendering and feature gates.
Pass every exported pair, including rejected ones, through editable conversion and geometry checks.
Visually inspect all source/crop/mask/weave rows and all nineteen predicted ROI overlays.
Run focused coordinate/component tests and repository check, lint, tests and build.

limitations: Previously inspected development photos and body predictions; not an unseen test.
Derived-mask checks are not true cutting-path accuracy.
This isolates use of the current prediction, not the ultimate value of learned localization.
No app integration, model export, push or deployment.
